## What this covers

The observational data produced by this honeypot and the derived views built
from it:

- `stats.json`, `geo.json`, `attack_techniques.json`, `llm_fallback.json`,
  `session_replay.json`, `manifest.json`, `heartbeat.json`
- `db/` — the published SQLite database and its shards
- `replays/*.cast` — terminal recordings in asciicast v2 format

## What this does NOT cover

**`data/samples/` — captured malware.** Those archives contain third-party
binaries collected from attackers. They are not this project's work and not
this project's to license; no permission to use, redistribute, or execute them
is granted or implied here, and their own copyright status is unknown and
unknowable. They are published for research inspection only, zipped with the
password `infected` so they cannot execute by accident. Handle accordingly.

**`kev.json`** is a compact mirror of CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities
catalogue, which is a US Government work in the public domain. It is
redistributed here for convenience and carries CISA's terms, not these.

## Read this before drawing conclusions from the data

Attribution satisfies the licence. It does not make a finding correct. This
dataset has properties that will mislead anyone who treats it as a
representative sample of internet attack traffic:

- **One sensor, one cloud, one region.** It observes what reaches a single
  AWS EC2 instance in us-east-1. It is not a sample of global attack traffic.
- **Session counts are dominated by a handful of hosts.** A small number of
  high-volume automated sources account for the overwhelming majority of
  sessions. Any session-weighted or event-weighted statistic is substantially
  a measurement of those hosts. Prefer counts of distinct source addresses.
- **Login success rates measure the honeypot's configuration**, not attacker
  capability. The honeypot accepts nearly any credential by design.
- **ATT&CK technique tags are pattern matches**, not verified classifications.
  Tags are assigned by regular expressions over command text. False negatives
  are far more likely than false positives, and a single high-volume automated
  behaviour can dominate a technique's count.
- **The published database stores a capped number of sessions per behaviour
  cluster.** Aggregate counts are the true totals; the individual session rows
  are a sample.

The methodology page at <https://ap6pack.github.io/dist/honeypot/> (About)
carries the current version of these caveats and takes precedence over this
summary.

## Source addresses

This dataset contains IP addresses observed attacking a honeypot. Many belong
to compromised third-party hosts — home routers, small-business servers — whose
owners are victims rather than attackers. Presence in this dataset is evidence
that traffic came from an address, not that its owner did anything wrong.

To request removal of an address, open an issue at
<https://github.com/Ap6pack/Ap6pack.github.io/issues>.
